content:
No call for this meeting due to clashing with other events/travel. Let's use this thread to stay up to date about the following:

ArkLib
Updates/Review/Merge of FRI / proximity gaps PRs which are all close to being finalised

  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/145
  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/137
  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/105

I will also merge https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/143 next Thursday at the latest, assuming no further comments about Vlad's point that the definition of LawfulInterleavedCode is weaker than the one in the Ligero paper. (Perhaps with some clean up of the sublemma folders, unsure how much effort this might take.)

Any updates to the Binius related PRs

  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/94
  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/100
  • https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/pull/102
    Quang and I will discuss these with Chung on Tuesday, but making a note of them here for completeness and hopefully we are in a position to review/merge these between now and the next regular meeting in a month

VCV-io
As discussed, let's opt to merge https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/VCV-io/pull/79 to make it easier to iterate on what remains to be done (filling in sorry's, etc) and tag VCV-io accordingly -- ArkLib will continue to use the v4.24.0-rc1 tag. May use v4.24.0-rc2 as a reminder to do this (bumping will produce a new tag automatically) or do it on Thursday 2nd at the latest unless we determine otherwise.

Iris-Lean
Nothing in particular to note here for now I think, should be fine to discuss in a month when work is closer to starting.

Computable Polynomials
Main todo is creating the new repo in https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM and populating it with the relevant material.

Hax Lean backend
Would be great to gather more feedback once the computable polynomial library is set up as we should be able to make an attempt to verify some examples from Jolt (and subsequently plonky3) against these as the first real test on representative Rust code.
@Clément Blaudeau I recall from when we chatted you had some progress on setting up the Lean tutorial page etc... if there are any examples/tutorial problems we could fill in please leave these here for us to look at and hopefully contribute! I think @Daniel Britten in particular expects to be looking at this (he has already looked into a previous iteration of the Lean backend in August as well as the existing Rocq backend to compare back then).

Let me know if there's anything I missed we should keep track of over the next month.

We've updated our tutorial on the Lean backend for Hax. If you have any feedback, I'll be very interested (here or on Hax's Zulip directly). Please try out the Lean backend and tell me how it goes. Make sure to use the lean-nightly branch for the latest features (the main is a few weeks behind).
Adding this to the Cargo.toml : 

hax-lib = { git = "https://github.com/cryspen/hax", branch = "lean-nightly" }

and, if you work on the extracted code, adding the Lean Hax prelude as a lake dependency 

[[require]]
name = "Hax"
git = { url = "git@github.com:cryspen/hax.git", subDir = "proof-libs/lean/" }
rev = "lean-nightly"

The Jolt core extraction (and script) is available on github

Hi @Clément Blaudeau, I've put some initial feedback here on Hax's Zulip.

I'll keep adding to that thread as I go. I've been on leave the last week and a half but now it's my primary focus :slight_smile:.
